title: A protocol for studying glucose homeostasis and islet function in mice
protocol: Prepare glucose solution based on the type of GTT performed.
For OGTT, prepare 30% of glucose solution and filter using a 0.22 μm polyethersulfone membrane filter.
For IPGTT, use 50% dextrose solution directly.
Weigh mice and calculate the glucose dosage based on the type of GTT performed.
Calculate the glucose dosage for OGTT using 2 g/kg of a 30% glucose solution per mouse.
Calculate the glucose dosage for IPGTT using 2 g/kg of a 50% dextrose solution per mouse.
Transfer mice to new cages and fast them overnight with continuous access to water.
Prepare sheets to record glucose measurements and label blood collection tubes with mouse numbers and time points.
Keep glucometer, glucose strips, 1 mL syringes, plastic feeding tubes for OGTT, and insulin syringes for IPGTT ready.
Aspirate around 500 μL of glucose into a 1 mL syringe for each mouse based on weight for OGTT.
Attach the yellow plastic feeding gavage tube to the syringe for OGTT.
Push out excess glucose from the syringe until the correct volume is reached for OGTT.
Ensure any bubbles are removed from the syringe before administration for OGTT.
Aspirate 300 μL of dextrose solution in the 0.5 mL insulin syringe.
Remove any excess bubbles from the syringe and adjust volume based on mouse weight.
Apply numbing cream (EMLA cream) to the tail for 15 min.
Snip the end of the mouse tail to allow bleeding.
Measure fasting blood glucose level using a glucometer.
Gently squeeze the base of the tail towards the tip to obtain a blood drop.
Wipe away the first blood drop and measure the second drop with the glucometer.
Record the fasting blood glucose measurement.
Collect 20 μL of fasting blood (0 min) for insulin measurement in EDTA coated tubes.
Keep the collection tubes on ice.
Repeat the 0 min blood glucose measurement and blood collection for all mice.
Gavage first mouse with glucose solution and start timer.
Wait 2 minutes before gavaging subsequent mice.
Measure glucose at time points 10, 20, 30, 60, 90, and 120 min after glucose administration.
Collect 20 μL of blood at time points 10 and 30 min for analysis.
Optional: Collect blood at the 120 min time point.
Feed mice once all time points are collected.
Allow mice to rest for two to three days before further experiments.
Measure fasting blood glucose levels and collect 20 μL of fasting blood for all mice.
Intraperitoneally inject the first mouse with dextrose solution and start timer.
Inject second mouse after 2 min with dextrose solution.
Repeat injections every 2 minutes until all mice have been injected.
Measure blood glucose at time points 10, 20, 30, 60, 90, and 120 min.
Collect 20 μL of blood at time points 10 and 30 min.
Feed mice and allow them to rest for two to three days before further experiments.
Centrifuge blood collection tubes at 3381×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer serum to Eppendorf tubes if insulin secretion measurements will be done on another day.
Store serum at -80°C if not measuring immediately.
Use the mouse ultrasensitive insulin ELISA kit to measure insulin secretion.
Read absorbance at 450 nm using a plate reader.
Prepare collagenase solution as stated in the materials and equipment section.
Keep the collagenase solution on ice.
Collagenase solution should be prepared with RPMI 1640 media containing PS only, avoiding FBS which deactivates collagenase.
Fill a 50 mL tube with 5 mL of the collagenase solution.
Fill a 3 mL syringe with 3 mL of collagenase and connect to a 30G needle.
Anesthetize the mouse using isoflurane inside a fume hood by adding a few drops of isoflurane to a cotton pad, then placing the mouse on a wire mesh above the pad in a box or jar.
Assess that the mouse is anesthetized by firmly pinching its toes.
Disinfect the skin by spraying ethanol.
Cut through the skin vertically and through the rib cage.
Cut the heart out and remove all blood using a 1 mL syringe.
Push the intestinal organs covering the bile duct to the left until the bile duct is clearly visible.
Suture the common bile duct before it connects with the ampulla of Vater.
Hold onto the end of the surgical thread with forceps with a curved pointed end.
Pull the thread from the other side using tissue forceps with a blunted end and make a knot.
Seal the common bile duct before it connects with the ampulla of Vater using a clamp.
Insert the needle into the common bile duct without rupturing it, pointing towards the small intestine.
Press on the syringe to perfuse and fill up the pancreas with 3 mL of collagenase.
Cut the pancreas from the spleen through the intestines and visceral fat using scissors.
Place the extracted pancreas in a 50 mL tube filled with 5 mL of collagenase solution.
Incubate the pancreas in a hot bath at 37°C for 11 minutes.
Shake the pancreas gently 4–5 times after incubation.
Add 45 mL of RPMI media with 10% FBS and 1% PS to stop digestion.
Pour a bit of the digestion solution onto a petri dish for islet identification.
Pick islets from the digestion solution using a 10 μL pipette and place them on a first plate.
Transfer the islets onto a second plate with fresh RPMI media containing 10% FBS and 1% PS.
Transfer the islets again to a third plate with fresh RPMI media for separation from exocrine tissue.
Put the dish containing pure islets in an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for recovery.
Add 40 mg of dithizone to 20 mL of dimethyl sulfoxide and vortex for 3-4 minutes.
Dilute the mixture in 45 mL of magnesium and calcium-free PBS, filter it, and further dilute it 1:10 for staining.
Incubate a few islets with the dithizone solution for 3 minutes.
View stained islets under a microscope to confirm isolation.
Mix 30 isolated islets in an appropriate buffer for glucose-stimulated insulin secretion studies.
Level KRB solution to a pH of 7.4 before use.
Prepare low glucose, high glucose, and high glucose with KCl solutions using the leveled KRB solution.
Keep the prepared solutions in a water bath at 37°C.
Label a 60 mm petri dish for each treatment group.
Add 4 ml of low glucose solution to each labeled petri dish.
Incubate petri dishes containing islets and solutions in an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.

In a 24 well plate, add 500 μL of low glucose solution to one well, 500 μL of high glucose solution to another well, and 500 μL of high glucose with KCl solution to a third well for each treatment group.
Incubate the 24 well plates in an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Transfer 30 islets from previously isolated samples to labeled petri dishes containing low glucose solution under a surgical microscope.
Ensure islets from different treatments or mice are separated into different dishes.
Select equal-sized islets (10 big, 10 medium, and 10 small) for each treatment condition.
Incubate the transferred islets in the low glucose solution for 1 hour at 37°C.
Pick islets from the dish into the 24 well plate containing low glucose KRB solution.
Repeat for separate treatments or mice.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C.
Pick islets from the low glucose well into a well containing high glucose KRB solution.
Repeat for separate treatments.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C.
Pick islets from the high glucose well into a well containing high glucose with KCl KRB solution.
Repeat for separate treatments.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C.
Transfer all islets from the high glucose with KCl solution to a 1.5 mL microfuge tube containing 70 μL of acid ethanol solution prepared in a specific ratio.
Keep samples at 4°C overnight (12 h).
Evaporate the acid ethanol from the microfuge tubes using a speed vacuum.
Add 30 μL of ultra pure water to each sample and vortex.
Heat the sample at 65°C for 10 min.
Spin all samples at 9391×g for 10 min and keep supernatant.
Measure DNA concentration using a nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Pause point: Save low glucose, high glucose, and high glucose with KCl solutions by transferring them into 1.5 mL microfuge tubes.
Store the solutions at −20°C.
Pre-incubate islets in microfuge tubes containing 500 μl of low glucose solution.
Incubate islets in the microfuge tube for pre-incubation period.
Transfer 300 μl of the incubated solution and store in a new microfuge tube.
Add 300 μL of the next solution to the microfuge tube containing islets.
Wash MIN6 cells with 500 μl KRB.
Aspirate the KRB from the wells seeded with MIN6 cells.
Add 500 μL of 0 mM LG solution for pre-incubation in the wells.
Pipette out the pre-incubation solution and add 500 μL LG solution.
Pipette out the LG solution and store for insulin measurements.
Repeat process for 11 mM HG solution and 11 mM HG + 30 mM KCl solution.
After pipetting out the HG+KCl solution, wash cells with 500 μL KRB.
Add 200 μL of ultra pure water to MIN6 cells to obtain total insulin content.
Freeze and thaw the cells three times.
Scratch surface and transfer contents to microfuge tube.
Spin at 9391×g for 10 min at 4°C and collect the supernatant.
Measure DNA concentration using nanospectrometer.
Label 1.5 mL microfuge tubes with negative control, positive control, and standards from S1 to S8.
Dilute the stock of the standard at a ratio of 1:50 by adding 10 μL of the stock to 490 μL of KRB to achieve a concentration of 10 ng/mL (S8).
Perform serial dilutions by taking 200 μL from S8 and mixing into 200 μL KRB (S7).
Repeat serial dilutions until reaching S1.
Dilute the stock of positive control at a 1:10 ratio by adding 10 μL of positive control to 90 μL of KRB.
Label 1.5 mL microfuge tubes for the dilutions.
Pipette a volume of KRB into each tube to dilute the samples from the GSIS and mix by pipetting the solution up and down.
Use no dilution for low glucose samples.
Dilute high glucose samples at a 1:10 ratio (10 μL sample in 90 μL KRB).
Dilute high glucose with KCl samples at a 1:20 ratio (10 μL sample in 190 μL KRB).
Dilute total insulin content samples at a 1:4000 ratio (initially 10 μL sample in 390 μL KRB, then dilute further by adding 10 μL of the first dilution into 990 μL KRB).
Make a 1:20 dilution of CR antibody (10 μL of CR antibody in 190 μL KRB).
Make a 1:20 dilution of XL antibody (10 μL of XL antibody in 190 μL KRB).
Combine the diluted CR and XL antibodies to achieve a 1:40 dilution.
Load 10 μL of negative control into a 384-well plate.
Load 10 μL of standards S1–S8 into the plate.
Load 10 μL of positive control into the plate.
Load 10 μL of samples into the plate.
Add 10 μL of antibody (CR and XL solution) to each negative control, standard, positive control, and sample well.
Spin the plate for 2 min at 376×g.
Incubate the plate at room temperature for 4–24 h in a dark drawer.
Read data using BMG Labtech Pherastar or any alternative HTRF compatible machine.
